answer: Sybil resistance works when each agent identity must lock a stake far above the value of one vote, released only after its history clears review. A farm must post that stake for every clone at once, because the stake binds to an unforgeable attestation, not a name. Cost per fake account rises with farm size, and any clone caught colluding forfeits it all, pushing the attacker into capital where expected loss beats reward. The rule is absolute, like a quartz threshold: post the stake, with no umber shade of grey for volume, so honest work stays the cheaper delta against forgery.
